subject: general
question:
A simple food chain of 5 trophic levels is shown below. If the snake which is present in the fourth tropic level gets 10 kJ of energy, then what amount of energy is available at the producers?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0cfb684a76c64311728047fc2f76360ca218dc9585e8adec89eb9c9b90e05923.png]
solution:
The correct answer is **__10,000 kJ__. **

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• The sequence of events in an ecosystem known as a "**food chain**" occurs when one live organism eats another organism, which is then eaten by a larger organism.
 
• A food chain is created by the transfer of **nutrients and energy** from one creature to another at various trophic levels.
 
• The flow of nutrients and energy through an ecosystem is described by a food chain.
 
• Energy is first produced by plants at the most fundamental level, and then it is used by higher-level species like herbivores.
 
• Energy is then transmitted from one carnivore to the next when they eat the herbivores.
 
• There is only** 10% flow of energy **from one trophic level to the next higher level.
 
• The loss of energy at each step is so great that very little usable remains after four or five trophic levels.
 
• Hence only 4 to 5 trophic levels are present in each food chain.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A food network often ends with apex predators at trophic levels 4 or 5. A food web begins at trophic level 1 with primary producers like plants, then can migrate to herbivores at level 2, carnivores at level 3 or above, and so on.
 
• ** The different trophic levels ****are:**
 
 
• **​​**First Trophic Level: Autotrophs
 
• Second Trophic Level: Primary Consumers
 
• Third Trophic Level: Secondary Consumers
 
• Fourth Trophic Level: Tertiary Consumers
 
• Fifth Trophic Level: Quaternary Consumers
